connections.description: Named connections: where data lives and how to sign in.

then.description:
Files in an Azure Blob Storage container.

With account, sign-in uses DefaultAzureCredential: your
az login locally, a managed identity in Azure, or service principal
environment variables. With connection_string, that string is used.
Step paths are relative to prefix within the container.
then.title: AzureBlobConfig
then.markdownDescription:
Files in an Azure Blob Storage container.

With `account`, sign-in uses `DefaultAzureCredential`: your
`az login` locally, a managed identity in Azure, or service principal
environment variables. With `connection_string`, that string is used.
Step paths are relative to `prefix` within the container.

then.description:
Azure SQL Database or SQL Server.

With server and database, sign-in uses an Entra ID token from
DefaultAzureCredential: your az login locally, a managed identity
in Azure. A fresh token is fetched for every new database connection, so
long runs aren't cut off when a token expires. With
connection_string, that ODBC connection string is used as it is.

Writes use pyodbc's fast_executemany.
then.title: AzureSQLConfig
then.markdownDescription:
Azure SQL Database or SQL Server.

With `server` and `database`, sign-in uses an Entra ID token from
`DefaultAzureCredential`: your `az login` locally, a managed identity
in Azure. A fresh token is fetched for every new database connection, so
long runs aren't cut off when a token expires. With
`connection_string`, that ODBC connection string is used as it is.

Writes use pyodbc's `fast_executemany`.

then.description:
Files on the local filesystem.

Step paths are relative to root, and a relative root is relative
to the folder you run from. Parent folders are
created when writing, and a file is written under a temporary name and
only then put in place, so a failed write leaves the old file untouched.
then.title: LocalConfig
then.markdownDescription:
Files on the local filesystem.

Step paths are relative to `root`, and a relative `root` is relative
to the folder you run from. Parent folders are
created when writing, and a file is written under a temporary name and
only then put in place, so a failed write leaves the old file untouched.

then.description:
Files in a SharePoint document library.

Signs in with DefaultAzureCredential, so the identity needs Graph
permission to the site's files (for example Sites.Selected or
Sites.ReadWrite.All for a service principal). Step paths are
relative to folder in library. Wildcards are allowed in file
names, not in folder names. Uploads are limited to 250 MB.
then.title: SharePointConfig
then.markdownDescription:
Files in a SharePoint document library.

Signs in with `DefaultAzureCredential`, so the identity needs Graph
permission to the site's files (for example `Sites.Selected` or
`Sites.ReadWrite.All` for a service principal). Step paths are
relative to `folder` in `library`. Wildcards are allowed in file
names, not in folder names. Uploads are limited to 250 MB.

then.description:
Any database SQLAlchemy supports, given a database URL.

A relative SQLite path is relative to the folder you run from, and
the folder for a new SQLite file is created.
